action: Mikey lived on four and was in JC's class. JC can't remember his score; he remembers what the mothers called it: 'the three', low, in the voice they used for a man who'd gone upstate. Mikey's mother said it most. Eight-year-old Mikey puts his ear to the fourth-floor stairwell wall and says the building is humming; he stays there long after a joke would be over. “Listen,” he says. JC listens to a wall and laughs at him. The wall hums in concentric gold rings. Present: JC has a microphone clamped to his own wall.
